content.text: In Nigeria, Stripe and PayPal are restricted, leaving digital creators without a way to process payments for their [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-how-sell-ebooks-kenya-complete-infrastructure-guide-5|ebooks]], courses, and software. This is a [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/problem-financial-sovereignty-digital-creators-crypto-how-solve|The Problem]] not just for Nigerians, but for anyone living in countries with similar restrictions. The infrastructure required to sell digital products internationally is often built with specific regions in mind, leaving behind those who need it most. By leveraging blockchain-based payments and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-every-detail-3|COREMERCH guide to cloudflare]] infrastructure, digital creators in Africa can now sell their digital products to anyone, anywhere in the world, without relying on platforms that are limited or blocked.

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail: Digital products

This infrastructure works because it's built on open standards and decentralized technologies. By using blockchain-based payments and Cloudflare infrastructure, digital creators can process payments and deliver their products without relying on platforms that are limited or blocked. This means that they can reach a global audience, without being held back by regional restrictions or fees. In contrast, platforms like Stripe and PayPal are designed to facilitate transactions within specific regions, and often come with fees and restrictions that can eat into a creator's profits. By choosing a more open and decentralized approach, digital creators can maintain full control over their products and their customer relationships, while also avoiding the fees and restrictions that come with traditional payment processing methods. For example, USDT on Tron settles in under 60 seconds for a fee under $0.10, making it an attractive option for creators who want to process transactions quickly and affordably.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you can deploy this infrastructure, you'll need a few key components. First, you'll need a digital product to sell - an ebook, a course, a software application, or something else entirely. You'll also need a way to host your product, which can be done using a platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Next, you'll need a payment gateway that can process transactions in a way that's compliant with your region's regulations. In some cases, you may also need to set up a delivery pipeline, which can be done using a platform like Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Finally, you'll need to choose a cryptocurrency that you can use for payment processing, such as USDT on Tron or Binance Coin on Binance Smart Chain. Once you have these components in place, you'll be ready to deploy your infrastructure and start selling your digital products to a global audience.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Setting up your payment and delivery pipeline is a critical step in deploying your infrastructure. This involves choosing a payment gateway that can process transactions in a way that's compliant with your region's regulations, and setting up a delivery pipeline that can securely deliver your products to your customers. In some cases, you may also need to set up a webhook that can notify your customers when their payment has been processed, and their product is ready for download. By setting up your payment and delivery pipeline correctly, you can ensure that your customers have a seamless and secure experience, while also avoiding any potential issues with payment processing or product delivery.
You can reach a global audience with blockchain-based payments and Cloudflare infrastructure.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you've set up your payment and delivery pipeline, it's time to go live and process your first transaction. This involves setting up your storefront, choosing a cryptocurrency for payment processing, and configuring your payment gateway to work with your chosen cryptocurrency. Once you've done this, you can start accepting payments from your customers, and delivering your products securely to their wallets. By going live and processing your first transaction, you'll be able to test your infrastructure and make any necessary adjustments before launching your digital products to a global audience.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Scaling your infrastructure is an important step in maintaining the performance and security of your digital commerce stack. This involves monitoring your traffic and usage patterns, and making any necessary adjustments to ensure that your infrastructure can handle the volume of transactions that you're expecting. By scaling your infrastructure correctly, you can ensure that your customers have a seamless and secure experience, while also avoiding any potential issues with payment processing or product delivery. In addition to scaling your infrastructure, you may also need to consider implementing additional security measures, such as two-factor authentication or IP blocking, to protect your customers and your business from potential threats.

Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your digital commerce stack, follow these steps: Set up a digital product to sell, such as an ebook or a software application. Choose a hosting platform, such as GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages. Select a payment gateway that can process transactions in a way that's compliant with your region's regulations. Set up a delivery pipeline, such as Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. Configure your payment gateway to work with your chosen cryptocurrency. Set up a webhook to notify your customers when their payment has been processed, and their product is ready for download. Choose a cryptocurrency for payment processing, such as USDT on Tron or Binance Coin on Binance Smart Chain. Test your infrastructure and make any necessary adjustments before launching your digital products to a global audience.
Frequently Asked Questions
Do I need to have technical expertise to deploy this infrastructure?

No, you don't need to have technical expertise to deploy this infrastructure. However, you will need to have a basic understanding of how to set up a digital commerce stack, and how to configure your payment and delivery pipeline. If you're not comfortable with these tasks, you may want to consider hiring a developer or a consultant to help you set up your infrastructure.
Can I use this infrastructure to sell physical products?

No, this infrastructure is designed specifically for selling digital products, such as ebooks, courses, and software applications. If you want to sell physical products, you'll need to use a different infrastructure that's designed for that purpose.
How do I handle refunds and disputes with this infrastructure?

Refunds and disputes can be handled manually by setting up a support system, or by using a third-party service that specializes in dispute resolution. It's also a good idea to have a clear refund and return policy in place to avoid any potential issues with customers who may not be satisfied with their purchases.
Can I use this infrastructure to sell products on a subscription basis?

Yes, you can use this infrastructure to sell products on a subscription basis. You'll need to set up a recurring payment schedule, and configure your payment gateway to process the recurring payments. You'll also need to have a clear subscription and cancellation policy in place to avoid any potential issues with customers who may not be satisfied with their subscriptions.
How do I integrate this infrastructure with my existing website or e-commerce platform?

You can integrate this infrastructure with your existing website or e-commerce platform by using APIs, or by using a third-party service that specializes in e-commerce integrations. You'll need to have a basic understanding of how to set up APIs, and how to configure your payment and delivery pipeline to work with your existing platform.
Can I use this infrastructure to sell products in multiple currencies?

Yes, you can use this infrastructure to sell products in multiple currencies. You'll need to set up a payment gateway that can process transactions in multiple currencies, and configure your payment gateway to work with your chosen currencies.
